ℹ️  ADR / GDR source attribution: Indian-company ADRs / GDRs (INFY, IBN, HDB, WIT, RDY, ...) carry US- / Jersey- / Cayman-prefixed ISINs and remain foreign-source for FSI/TR/Form 67 under the depositary convention. If your CA prefers the underlying-issuer view, set [os].schedule_os_indian_adr_routing = 'underlying-issuer'. Either mode leaves the Schedule OS 1a(i) total unchanged.
ℹ️  No in-FY foreign-source short-term capital gains found in FY 2025-26; wrote zero-row review CSV with TOTAL ₹0.
ℹ️  No in-FY foreign-source long-term capital gains found in FY 2025-26; wrote zero-row review CSV with TOTAL ₹0.
ℹ️  ADR / GDR routing note: Indian-company ADRs / GDRs are treated as foreign-source per the asset-as-held convention (default 'depositary' mode). Their dividends appear in the FSI under their depositary's source country (typically US / Jersey / Cayman), and any depositary-country WHT is layered onto the matching same-country row. If your CA prefers the underlying-issuer view, set [os].schedule_os_indian_adr_routing = 'underlying-issuer' in user.toml — the FSI compute layer symmetrically excludes the mapped Indian-ADR WHT to prevent silent absorption (issue #225 fix in PR #251).
⚠️  Schedule TR tax relief and section are LEFT BLANK — not auto-populated (no verified DTAA path or incomplete §91 evidence). Supply exact Form 67 evidence where applicable and fill manually before filing.
Form 67 CSV importer may blank fractional Rate(%) 15.38 for country code 2; after upload, enter 15.38 manually and verify it before saving. Do not round it to an integer.

ℹ️  Form 67 DTAA article + rate (cols 9-10) populated, but cols 7 and 11-13 remain blank until exact Indian tax attributable to the source is supplied.

⚠️  Account ID cross-check was SKIPPED because the input statement masked the account number AND masked-account acceptance is enabled (--allow-masked-account or [account].allow_masked_account in user.toml). You are responsible for confirming the statement belongs to the same account as user.toml before filing.

ℹ️  Foreign Taxpayer Identification Number is BLANK for one or more countries where foreign tax was paid. On Schedule FSI / TR this number is generally MANDATORY when claiming foreign-tax relief under section 90 / 90A / 91 — leaving it blank can delay processing or cause the relief to be denied. The IBKR statement does not carry your foreign TIN, so add it to user.toml under [account.foreign_tins], keyed by the country's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. US = "123456789"; run `ibkr-fa init` for an annotated template), then re-run — one entry fills BOTH Schedule FSI and Schedule TR. If that country did not allot you a TIN, enter your passport number instead.

⚠️  INDIAN TAX CALCULATION REQUIRED: Schedule FSI column (d) and Form 67 column 7 are left blank where Indian tax attributable to foreign income cannot be derived from broker data. Rule 128(5)(i) limits FTC to the lower of Indian tax payable on that income and eligible foreign tax, but does not prescribe an average or marginal-rate formula. For ordinary income, Promac Engineering v ACIT (ITA 501/Bang/2018, paras 12-13) applied `foreign income x average Indian tax rate`; section 2(10) defines that average as `Indian income-tax on total income / total income`. Promac was for pre-Rule-128 AY 2014-15, and the Karnataka High Court later disposed the Revenue's appeal on monetary limits with the legal question kept open; no reported ruling was found settling average versus marginal rate under Rule 128(5)(i). Do not substitute foreign tax withheld. Confirm the method under the relevant DTAA/current law and any special-rate treatment, then enter the result manually. To have the tool fill it, add an exact [[form67.tax_payable_overrides]] amount for the country's DIVIDEND row and, when its Schedule FSI Other Sources row also holds interest or other income, one for INTEREST_INCOME or OTHERS too.

⚠️  **Black Money Act disclosure reminder**: Under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015, you (as an Indian resident) MUST disclose every foreign asset and every foreign income source on ITR-2 each assessment year. Filing an ITR but omitting the Schedule FA disclosure can trigger a flat ₹10 lakh penalty under Section 43, irrespective of the tax position. Since Finance (No.2) Act, 2024 (effective 1 October 2024), Section 43 has a ₹20 lakh aggregate-value carve-out covering ALL foreign assets other than immovable property — the penalty does not apply where the aggregate value of such assets does not exceed ₹20 lakh at any time during the relevant previous year (the statutory test is a peak-balance test against the previous year, not a year-end snapshot). Wilful non-disclosure additionally carries 6 months to 7 years rigorous imprisonment under Section 50; Finance Act, 2026 (Act 4 of 2026; Presidential assent 30 March 2026) inserted a matching ₹20 lakh aggregate-foreign-asset (other than immovable property) proviso to Section 50 (and Section 49), deemed to have been inserted with effect from 1 October 2024 — so the Section 50 carve-out now mirrors the Section 43 carve-out at the same threshold and effective date.
   Undisclosed foreign income / asset value attracts a flat 30% tax under Section 3, and a penalty of 300% of that tax (~90% of the undisclosed value) under Section 41 — for a combined exposure of ~120% of the undisclosed value, in addition to the Section 43 fixed penalty and any Section 50 prosecution.
   The Schedule FA / OS / CG output ibkr-fa produces is the *mechanically correct* disclosure; the *decision to file* the return is yours. Do not defer filing without consulting a CA familiar with foreign-asset disclosure. RNOR (resident-but-not-ordinarily-resident) assessees have a Section 2 carve-out; current Indian residents (the default for someone living in India ≥ 2 years) are squarely in scope. Note that the 2019 retrospective amendment (Finance Act, 2019) extends BMA to non-residents / NRIs in respect of foreign assets acquired *while they were resident* — consult a CA before assuming non-resident status fully exempts you.
   This advisory fires on every ibkr-fa subcommand run and cannot be silenced via --quiet (tax-safety diagnostics are non-quietable by design).

ℹ️  **ITR form selection**: Foreign-asset / foreign-income holders cannot use ITR-1 (Sahaj) or ITR-4 (Sugam) — both form headers explicitly exclude anyone with assets located outside India. The two applicable forms are:
   * **ITR-2** — default for ibkr-fa users. Use if your income consists of salary + house property + capital gains + foreign assets / income + other sources, with NO business or profession income.
   * **ITR-3** — required if you ALSO have business or profession income (intraday equity trading, F&O / derivatives, freelance / consulting fees, professional income, partnership-firm distributive share, ...). A presumptive-scheme filer under §44AD/44ADA/44AE who would otherwise use ITR-4 also falls back to ITR-3 once they hold foreign assets.
   Long-term and short-term capital gains from delivery-based equity (the ibkr-fa use case) are *typically* NOT business income and remain in ITR-2 territory when treated as capital assets / investments — but CBDT Circular 6/2016 recognises that listed shares can ALSO be held as stock-in-trade, in which case the gains become business income and ITR-3 applies. The fact-specific tests (frequency, intent, treatment in books) outside the >12-month safe harbor put the burden on the assessee; if you actively trade your foreign equity as a business, treat the income as business income and use ITR-3. Intraday equity trades are speculative transactions under Section 43(5), generally reported as speculative business income. Section 43(5) proviso (d) excludes eligible derivatives on a prescribed/notified recognised stock exchange from that speculative definition; foreign-exchange derivatives do not automatically qualify. Either business classification pushes you to ITR-3. ibkr-fa cannot tell from your IBKR statement alone whether you have business income elsewhere; this is your call. When in doubt, consult a CA.
